Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Disclosed herein are a storage unit (250) and a secure delivery system (200) that uses such a storage unit. The storage unit (250) includes a plurality of compartments (254, 256) including at least one refrigerated compartment (256), wherein each refrigerated compartment (256) is associated with a thermostat and a cooling device. The storage unit (250) also includes a corresponding plurality of scales (258, 260), each compartment being associated with a scale, a communications module (262) for coupling to a communications network (205), at least one lid (820) for accessing the compartments (254, 256), and a lock adapted to secure each lid (820) in a closed position. The storage unit (250) further includes a control panel (810) for controlling the lock, wherein the control panel (810) has a user interface for receiving input from a user, and a power source for supplying power to the cooling device and the control panel. The control panel (810) is adapted to release the lock upon validating the received input against a code received by the communications module (262).

The storage unit (250) contains multiple compartments (254, 256), at least one of which is refrigerated (256). outputs.L3:
The disclosed secure delivery system includes a storage unit divided into multiple compartments, at least one of which is refrigerated. Each refrigerated compartment is equipped with a thermostat and an associated cooling device to maintain a desired temperature. In addition, every compartment is paired with a scale, enabling the system to detect or monitor the presence and weight of stored items.

The storage unit further includes a communications module configured to connect to a communications network, allowing the system to receive access codes or other relevant information remotely. Access to the compartments is controlled by at least one lid, which is secured in a closed position by a lock.

A powered control panel manages access to the storage unit. When a user enters information through the control panel, the system validates that input against a code received through the communications module. If the entered information matches the received code, the control panel causes the lock to release, thereby permitting access to the applicable compartment or compartments.
outputs.L4:
A secure delivery system includes a network-connected storage unit designed to receive, protect, and monitor delivered items until they are retrieved by an authorized user. The storage unit contains multiple individual compartments, allowing separate deliveries to be stored at the same time. Each compartment is equipped with a scale or other weight sensor that detects the presence, removal, or possible tampering of an item. One or more compartments may also include thermostat-controlled refrigeration components so that groceries, medications, and other temperature-sensitive goods can be maintained within a selected temperature range.

Each compartment has a locking lid or door that prevents unauthorized access. The locks, scales, temperature controls, and related sensors are connected to a powered control panel. The control panel may include a keypad, touchscreen, card reader, scanner, or other input device through which a delivery person or recipient enters identifying information. A communications module connects the system to a remote server, delivery service, property owner, or authorized user through a wired or wireless network.

When a delivery is scheduled, the system receives a temporary access code or other authentication credential through the communications module. The control panel compares the information entered by the user with the received credential. If the information matches, the control panel unlocks the appropriate compartment while leaving the remaining compartments secured. The system may then detect the placement or removal of an item using the compartment’s scale, relock the compartment, and transmit confirmation of the transaction.

The system can maintain an electronic record of access attempts, compartment status, item weight, and temperature conditions. It may also send alerts when a delivery is completed, an item is collected, a temperature moves outside an acceptable range, a lid is left open, or unauthorized access is attempted. By combining network-based authentication, individually secured compartments, weight monitoring, and controlled refrigeration, the system provides a convenient and reliable way to manage unattended deliveries while protecting items from theft, tampering, spoilage, and environmental exposure.
outputs.L5: The company disclosed the details of its new sustainability plan during the annual meeting. counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a secure delivery storage unit with multiple compartments, including a refrigerated compartment, individual scales, network connectivity, lockable lids, a user control panel, and code-based access validation.
counterfactuals.output: A secure delivery storage unit includes a housing defining a plurality of independently accessible compartments, at least one of which comprises a refrigerated compartment. Each compartment includes a support surface associated with an individual scale configured to detect the presence, removal, or weight of a delivered item. Respective lockable lids selectively restrict access to the compartments. A controller is operatively coupled to the scales, the locks, a user control panel, and a network communication interface. The network communication interface enables communication with a remote delivery, monitoring, or user-management system. The user control panel receives an access code or other identifying information, and the controller validates the received information against locally stored or remotely obtained authorization data. Upon successful validation, the controller unlocks one or more designated lids while maintaining the remaining compartments in a locked condition. Scale data, access events, compartment status, and refrigeration status may be recorded or transmitted to facilitate delivery confirmation, security monitoring, inventory tracking, and temperature-controlled storage.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical disclosure describing a smart parcel locker for grocery deliveries that monitors compartment weight, keeps selected items refrigerated, and unlocks when the user enters a code received over a communications network. Include reference numerals.
counterfactuals.output:
A smart parcel locker (100) for grocery deliveries includes a housing (102) defining one or more storage compartments (104). Each compartment (104) includes a door (106), an electronically controllable lock (108), and a weight sensor (110) configured to measure the weight of items placed in the compartment. A controller (112) receives weight data from the weight sensor (110) and determines whether an expected delivery has been deposited, removed, or changed.

At least one compartment (104) includes a refrigeration unit (114), such as a thermoelectric or compressor-based cooling device, and a temperature sensor (116). The controller (112) selectively operates the refrigeration unit (114) to maintain a set temperature for designated perishable items. Non-refrigerated compartments may remain at ambient temperature.

A network interface (118) communicates through a communications network (120) with a remote delivery platform or user device (122). Upon assignment or completion of a delivery, the controller (112) receives or generates an access code, which is transmitted to the user device (122). A user enters the access code through an input interface (124), such as a keypad or touchscreen. After validating the entered code, the controller (112) actuates the lock (108) to unlock the corresponding door (106). The controller (112) may further report weight, temperature, door, and access status to the remote platform and generate an alert if the measured weight or temperature falls outside a predetermined range.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

**Abstract**

A secure delivery system (200) includes a network-connected storage unit (250) configured to receive and temporarily store food deliveries. The storage unit (250) communicates through a communications module (262) with users, delivery personnel, and remote services over a network (205). Separate compartments (254, 256) accommodate respective food items and may maintain different environmental conditions. Scales (258, 260) associated with the compartments (254, 256) detect placement, removal, and weight changes of stored items. A lid (820) selectively restricts access to the compartments (254, 256), while a control panel (810) receives authentication information, displays delivery status, and controls locking or unlocking of the lid (820). counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for securely receiving unattended deliveries in temperature-controlled compartments, emphasizing thermostat-controlled refrigeration, weight sensing, remote code communication, a user interface, a power source, and electronic lock release after code verification.
counterfactuals.output:
A secure unattended-delivery receptacle includes one or more insulated, temperature-controlled compartments for receiving groceries, pharmaceuticals, or other perishable goods. Each compartment has a thermostat-controlled refrigeration system that maintains a selected temperature and a weight sensor that detects placement, removal, or changes in the delivered load.

A controller communicates through a wired or wireless network with a remote service, merchant, courier, or owner to receive and validate a delivery access code. A user interface, such as a keypad, touchscreen, scanner, or mobile-device interface, allows a courier to enter or transmit the code and provides status and operating instructions. After verifying the code, the controller electronically releases the lock for an authorized compartment. Once the delivery is detected by the weight sensor and the door is closed, the compartment automatically relocks and may send confirmation to the owner or remote service.

The receptacle is powered by a mains connection, battery, solar supply, or a combination thereof, optionally with backup power to preserve refrigeration, communications, sensing, and locking functions during an outage.
